findings.reason: a repair whose own evidence shows an unidentified live mechanism removing its target needs either a precondition that the §52 investigation has named that mechanism or a done-when clause requiring its guard, and the plan carries neither.
findings.text: §5 opens "The cause of the stall and of the fall is under investigation in §52, so this section starts once no §52 run is writing the graph", but the stated gate is only that writers stop, while neither the precondition nor the done-when requires the demotion mechanism to be identified or guarded; the record §5 cites separates the two quantities, reporting 105 names with accepted documentation under the run's exact ID against a net fall of 340, so something other than the drain is actively removing accepted documentation while §5 restores it, and §5's done-when would pass on a count that falls again at the next read

findings.reason: the ceiling is a number a later node must invent from an undefined term, and the two defensible choices differ enough to decide whether §4 can run at all.
findings.text: §5 fixes its ceiling as "the measured documentation rate times the backlog read then, plus a quarter" without saying which measured rate, and the drain record it cites supports two bases five times apart: 105 names with accepted documentation under the run's exact ID for USD 11.14, or the 21 of those the record says "lacked accepted documentation at the baseline"; at a backlog of 926 names the high basis puts the ceiling above the whole remaining USD 350 approval, and because §4's limit subtracts §5's ceiling, that reading can size §4 to nothing

findings.reason: the escalation path itself is stated and correct, so a larger starting backlog still reaches the lead; the clause reads as exceptional when it will be routine, which is wording rather than mechanism.
findings.text: §5 reserves spend at §4's dispatch from "the backlog read then", which by construction cannot contain the roughly 300 accepted names §4 itself creates and each of which needs documentation, so a starting backlog larger than the one the ceiling was cut on is the ordinary case rather than the exception its escalation clause is written as
